answer: Bonded stake forces every agent to lock verifiable value on-chain before earning rewards. Each identity posts a crystal-clear deposit visible to peers. An attacker spawning thousands of puppets must fund each at the summit of registration, so cost scales linearly with fake identities. Unlike a quill forging one signature, the bond stays in escrow and is slashed when collusion is detected. Attackers must outspend honest agents to reach a voting threshold. Proven coordination triggers confiscation, turning each puppet into a liability as bonded value rises and capture costs climb.
